# Start Here for Implementing Dependency Controls

If your build is stable but you want to take deliberate control of it, to align versions, remove a library, enforce a policy, or make builds reproducible, start here. Pick the outcome you want and jump to the mechanism that provides it.

### JVM: Maven (MS), Gradle (GS), sbt (SB)

Each scenario is implemented for all three tools. Jump to the version for your build tool.

- Align versions across projects → MS3/GS3/SB3: Dependency Management (BOM / Platform)
- Override a transitive version → MS6/GS6/SB6: Forcing a Version
- Override what a BOM provides → MS4/GS4/SB4: Hardcoded Version vs Managed Version
- Remove a transitive dependency from one path → MS5/GS5/SB5: Exclusions
- Keep an artifact out of the whole build → MS18/GS18/SB18: Banning a Dependency
- Replace one library with another → MS15/GS15/SB15: Substitution
- Ensure reproducible builds → MS11/GS11/SB11: Dependency Locking
- Block a known-bad version → MS14/GS14/SB14: Rejecting a Version
- Reduce runtime or classpath footprint → MS7/GS7/SB7: Scopes, also MS8/GS8/SB8: Optional Dependencies
- Use vendor-patched or private artifacts → MS16/GS16/SB16 (BOM) or MS17/GS17/SB17 (direct patch)

### Python: pip, Poetry, uv (P)

- Pin all versions for reproducibility → P5: Lock Files
- Constrain versions centrally → P6: Constraints Files
- Reject or override a version → P4: Specifiers (`!=`), P9: Exclusions: The Gap (uv overrides and exclusions)
- Separate optional and dev dependencies → P7: Extras and Dependency Groups
- Isolate project environments → P10: Virtual Environment Isolation
- Use a private index safely → P11: Private Index and Dependency Confusion
- Find vulnerable dependencies → P12: Auditing the Environment

### Node: npm, pnpm, Yarn (N)

- Lock all versions for reproducibility → N5: Lock Files
- Override a transitive version → N6: Overrides and Resolutions
- Manage a monorepo → N10: Workspaces and Monorepos
- Keep dev tooling out of production → N7: Dependency Types
- Enforce a single shared copy of a library → N8: Peer Dependencies
- Use a private registry safely → N11: Private Registry and Dependency Confusion
- Find vulnerable or abandoned packages → N12: Auditing the Tree
